commands.review_summary:
The PR makes browser response capture prefer precise `[data-testid^="conversation-turn"]` containers before falling back to the broad conversation-turn selector.

Reproducibility: Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes from source inspection: a reused conversation with prior turns can make `verifyPromptCommitted` return a broad committed-turn count that exceeds the new precise assistant turn index.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] The remaining blocker is a narrow selector-consistency repair that automation can attempt on the PR branch.

target.title: fix(browser): stop broad turn selector from blocking image/snapshot capture
target.body:
## Problem

Browser-mode runs that produce **image-only replies** (e.g. `--generate-image`) never complete: `waitForAssistantResponse` polls forever (`Waiting for ChatGPT response …`), even though the image has clearly finished rendering in ChatGPT. The session eventually times out and no artifact is captured.

## Root cause

`CONVERSATION_TURN_SELECTOR` is a broad 9-clause fallback:

```
article[data-testid^="conversation-turn"], div[data-testid^="conversation-turn"], section[data-testid^="conversation-turn"],
article[data-message-author-role], div[data-message-author-role], section[data-message-author-role],
article[data-turn], div[data-turn], section[data-turn]
```

On current ChatGPT DOM, a turn's outer container is `<section data-testid="conversation-turn-N">`, and the user message has a **nested** `<div data-message-author-role="user">` inside it. The broad selector matches both, so it **double-counts** turns. Concretely, for a fresh conversation with 2 real turns (user + assistant):

| Selector | Match count |
|---|---|
| `[data-testid^="conversation-turn"]` (precise) | **2** ✅ |
| `CONVERSATION_TURN_SELECTOR` (broad) | **3** ❌ |

This breaks the `minTurnIndex` gate. `readConversationTurnCount()` reads the baseline **before** submit, using the broad selector, and returns an inflated count (e.g. 3). The assistant reply's real `turnIndex` (e.g. 1) is then `1 < 3`, so `readAssistantSnapshot` discards **every** snapshot via:

```ts
if (turnIndex < minTurnIndex) return null;
```

Image replies are hit first because they have no text echo for the baseline-recovery path to fall back on; the snapshot is permanently suppressed and the poller loops until timeout. (Text replies can also be affected on resume/reused conversations where the baseline inflation compounds with prior history.)

I confirmed this end-to-end via CDP: on the live page, the broad selector returned 3 turns while the precise one returned 2, and the assistant turn lived at index 1 — permanently below `minTurnIndex=3`.

## Fix

Prefer the precise `[data-testid^="conversation-turn"]` container selector, falling back to the broad selector only when no testid containers exist (preserving the original behavior for older DOM shapes / project view). Applied at the 4 places that must keep baseline count and assistant turnIndex in sync:

1. `readConversationTurnCount` — baseline (the source of `minTurnIndex`)
2. `buildAssistantExtractor` — assistant turnIndex extraction
3. `isLastAssistantTurnFinished` — completion check in the response observer
4. the markdown-fallback scanner — last-assistant-turn lookup

The existing `CONVERSATION_TURN_SELECTOR` is **kept** as the fallback; nothing about the architecture changes. This is a strictly additive, minimal fix.

## Verification

- `pnpm run typecheck` ✅
- `tests/browser/assistantResponseStatus.test.ts` (18 tests) ✅
- Full browser suite: no new failures (the 3 pre-existing `pageActions` model-selector failures are unrelated and present on `main`)
- **End-to-end smoke** (manual, `--engine browser --model 5.5 --generate-image`): pre-fix the run polled forever past image completion; post-fix the image was captured and saved in ~2m25s:
  ```
  Generated 1 image(s). Saved to: .../oracle-test-cat.png
  status: completed
  ```

## Changes

- `src/browser/constants.ts`: add `CONVERSATION_TURN_CONTAINER_SELECTOR` (precise) with a comment explaining the double-count trap.
- `src/browser/index.ts`: `readConversationTurnCount` prefers the precise selector.
- `src/browser/actions/assistantResponse.ts`: the 3 turn scanners prefer the precise selector.

3 files, +35 / −6.
